name: Glassmorphism
visualIdentity: Normalized frosted-glass interface look: translucent panels, thin borders, soft shadows, restrained highlights, and visible background color. Keep text crisp and contrast readable; use blur sparingly. The suggested cool palette is optional, not canonical.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to simple layered UI cards over color. Suggested combinations extend it to app demos and SaaS onboarding with product-state motion, or analytics dashboards with charts inside glass panels. Inferred suitability: product explainers and concise data presentations where depth supports content.
limitations: Avoid hiding needed copy, stacking more than two blur layers, or placing charts on a busy gradient. Check contrast on the composited surface. Provide a solid-fill fallback when backdrop filtering is unsupported or transparency is reduced. Glass may confuse topics without interface content. Do not use fixed palette suggestions over supplied colors.
palette: Optional new-artwork tokens: background #182837, foreground #F6F7F0, accents #7AAEB4 and #A698C5 (four base colors). Optional Lab gradient between accents is for the background behind glass only. Preserve task, brand, reference, semantic, and asset colors exactly; do not auto-adjust or expand them. Opaque text pair checks meet 4.5:1, but do not establish contrast over glass, imagery, highlights, shadows, or video; inspect actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Animate panels, masks, and modest parallax; keep blur layers restrained. Video motion must be deterministic and seekable from composition time. For interactive HTML, compatible patterns include keyboard-operable product-state expansion, scroll-driven card stacks or chapters, swipe/keyboard carousels, pointer tilt with neutral return, and staged storytelling. These are optional patterns, not inherent glass behavior; honor reduced motion and readable holds.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory audio layer. Choose music, narration, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and user requirements. Voice-card playback, waveforms, and spatial panning are separate optional features; tilt alone does not imply audio. Use authorized assets and verify intelligibility, balance, clipping, and sync.
assetRequirements: Use available fonts and assets; load local fonts and assets before rendering. Audio or waveform displays require actual authorized audio; chart values must be verified. For image lightboxes, provide accurate dimensions, responsive sources, fallbacks, alternatives, and usable navigation. Other specific asset requirements are unspecified.
combinations: Use alone for simple layered cards. Pair with style-095 for product-state transitions and feedback, or style-097 for charts and metrics; keep charts on a more opaque fill and accents limited to the primary colors. Avoid aurora or other translucent styles that duplicate glass. Optional card stacking, chapter handoffs, carousels, voice-card tilt, and storytelling patterns should be used only when their content and geometry support them.
productionApproach: HTML/CSS owns glass rendering via backdrop-filter, translucent fills, borders, and shadows; SVG supplies scalable shapes, icons, masks, or charts. Select one motion owner per property. HyperFrames is the primary video assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified required limitation exists, recording why. Neither dictates visual design. Drive video state from seekable time, inspect browser filter behavior and rendered frames, and keep specialist rendering and motion logic separate.
